_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 3 Programs and Repeats. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order: the plan and the program, building and running, the repeat block, same output fewer blocks, test as you go, and where children really build these. Every count a repeat makes and every place the cat ends up comes from the kit - ART.program.expand and ART.run - so the film cannot disagree with the lesson about what a repeat does.
title: Programs and Repeats
subtitle: Grade 2 Computing
objectives: Understand that programs instruct computers how to run algorithms.
Know how to recreate algorithms as programs.
Know how to develop programs to produce desired outputs, including the use of the repeat command.
Identify the benefits of regularly testing programs throughout their development.

beats.say: Jump, jump, jump. Three blocks to make the cat jump three times.
Now say it with a repeat block. Repeat 3 times, jump. Two blocks.
An algorithm is the plan. It is the steps, written for a person.

at.steps: the steps, written for a person

beats.say: Move right. Jump. Say hello. That is an algorithm, in words.
A program is the same plan, built out of blocks the computer can follow.
The move right block, the jump block, the say hello block.
Now a computer can run it. The program says how to run the algorithm.

at.run: Now a computer can run it

beats.say: Write the algorithm first, in words. Then build it in blocks.
Take each step of the algorithm and place its block, in order.
Jump, jump, move left. Two jump blocks, then the move left block.
Then press Run. The cat does the blocks one at a time.
Watching it run is how you test it. Did the cat do exactly that?

at.did: Did the cat do exactly that?

beats.say: Here is a new kind of block. This one is the repeat block.
The repeat block repeats the block that comes after it.
Repeat 3 times, jump. The cat jumps three times, from two blocks.
The repeat block always goes before the block it repeats.
Put it after the jump, and nothing is repeated. It needs a block after it.
Some apps have a repeat that holds several blocks. This one repeats just the next one.
Jump, jump, jump and repeat 3 times, jump do exactly the same thing.
The output is what a program makes happen. Three jumps, both ways.
The second program is shorter, and shorter is easier to read and fix.
Careful, though. Repeat 2 times, move right is only two moves.
Move right, move right, move right is three. Count what the cat does.

at.moves: Move right, move right, move right

beats.say: Build ten blocks, run it once at the end, and it goes wrong.
The bug could be in any of the ten. That is ten places to look.
Now build two blocks, run it, check. Build two more, and run it again.
If it goes wrong now, the bug can only be in the last two.
Programmers test regularly, all the way through. The bug is in the newest bit.
These blocks work like the ones in ScratchJr, a real app on a tablet.
You choose a character, you choose a background, then you drag blocks together.
Your repeat 3 times is a loop block with a 3 in it. The green flag is Go.
A program tells the computer how to run an algorithm.
The repeat block goes before the block it repeats.
Same output, fewer blocks. And test as you go, every time.
